reason: Windows-compatibility-layer tooling (Wine itself and its many real forks/variants — wine-cachyos, wine-asahi-git, WineZGUI, ...) — verified live: no upstream category source ever covers these, but the family is coherent and unambiguous by name.
Proton (Valve's own Wine fork) and its real variants/managers — proton-cachyos-native, ProtonUp-Qt, ProtonPlus, ... — same Windows-compatibility-layer family as wine*, verified live.
Bottles, a real standalone Wine-prefix manager, plus its bottles-unwrapped build variant.
Lutris, a real standalone open-gaming-platform launcher, plus its real build variants/frontends (lutris-unwrapped, lutris-gamepad-ui-git, ...).
Steam and its real companion launchers/tools (Steam Link, steam-appimage, steam-acolyte, ...) — same "Windows/game-launching tooling" family as wine*/proton*/lutris*/bottles*.

Brother's own per-printer-model CUPS/LPR driver packages (brother-dcp-l2660dw, brother-hll2360d, ...) — verified live: 556 real matches, every one a driver for a specific real Brother printer/scanner model, no upstream category source ever covers these.

QEMU's own per-target-architecture emulator binaries (qemu-user-riscv64, qemu-system-s390x-hwe, ...) — verified live: each one a real, independently launchable emulator, not a library; no upstream category source covers these.

Docker's own ecosystem of real standalone CLI tools (docker-compose, docker-autocompose, dockerfmt, docker-machine-driver-*, ...) — verified live: predominantly real, independently launchable tools; a minority are shell-completion/credential-helper companions, accepted the same way Wine/Proton's own companion packages are.

openSUSE YaST2's own per-subsystem configuration modules (yast2-bootloader, yast2-auth-client, yast2-apparmor, ...) — verified live: each one a real, distinct configurable subsystem reachable from the YaST control center, same "system configuration" concept as DesktopSettings/HardwareSettings already map to. yast2-trans-<lang> translation packages are excluded separately (filter/rules.ts), not classified.

INDI's own per-device astronomy driver packages (indi-orion-ssg3, indi-gpsnmea, indi-limesdr, ...) — verified live: 135 real matches, every one a driver for a specific real telescope/camera/GPS/etc. device; requires the hyphen so it doesn't catch unrelated "indicator"/"indicators" packages.

MATLAB itself (a real, well-known numerical-computation app with no upstream category since it's proprietary/AUR-only) plus its real toolboxes (matlab-dipimage, ...) — the per-release GCC-version-pin meta-packages riding the same prefix are excluded separately (filter/rules.ts), not classified.

Product decision (2026-08-31): 'To Classify' must trend toward zero, not sit at the vast majority of the catalog — an approximate-but-plausible category beats none. Python's own PyPI-mirror package family (python-*, python3-*, python313-*, ...) is overwhelmingly libraries/bindings, previously left unclassified specifically because filter/rules.ts's exclusion logic couldn't trust it (real CLI tools like python3-pip ride the same prefix) — but a library is still a developer-facing artifact either way, so Developer Tools is a defensible category even where it isn't a launchable app. 28,781 real matches.
Alpine's own Python-binding prefix, same reasoning as python*.
